newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraqi paper attacks U.S., Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi paper attacks U.S., Turkey.

text.p: An Iraqi newspaper on Wednesday lashed out at the United States for keeping troops in the Gulf region and lambasted Turkey for its latest incursion into northern Iraq.

"In reality, the presence of American military troops in the region with this intensity was and still is a source of terror to the region's peoples...and a factor threatening their security and stability," al-Thawra, organ of the ruling Baath party, said in a front-page editorial.

In a separate commentary on Ankara's stand towards Iraq, Thawra said: "The pretexts which the Turkish government mentions for violating Iraq's sovereignty and the integrity of its land and airspace are not only silly and flimsy but planned to serve the anti-Iraq policy the United States pursues."
Thawra's editorial was a reaction to a statement it said a U.S. spokesman made recently in which he said Iraq was still a threat to international peace and security.
"As far as Iraq is concerned this statement, which is not based on any objective criterion, is yet another attempt to mislead American public opinion," Thawra said.
It said the accusation was meant to justify the presence of U.S. troops in the Gulf and Turkey and the continuation of sanctions on Iraq imposed for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
Regarding Ankara, Thawra urged Turkish officials to translate their positive words on relations with Iraq into deeds and free their policies from U.S. influence.

Last month Ankara renewed the mandate of a U.S. and British force protecting rebel Kurds in northern Iraq. On New year's Eve, Turkey sent troops backed by air support into northern Iraq in pursuit of anti-Ankara Kurdish separatist rebel.

"The repeated violation by Turkish troops of...Iraq's land and security is a rejected action and a flagrant breach of the U.N. Charter, international law and relations of good-neighbourliness," Thawra said.
